questions.question: How does the guide define Risk in cybersecurity terms?
options: Risk = Only the size of the company
Risk = Only the cost of a firewall
Risk = Only the number of employees
questions.explanation: Risk = Threat × Vulnerability × Impact — identify karo kya risks hain, kitni probability hai, agar hua to kitna damage.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the four ways to treat a risk, according to the guide?
questions.explanation: Decide karo accept karo, mitigate karo, transfer karo (insurance) ya avoid karo — 'Ignore' formal risk treatment option nahi hai.

questions.question: Why is it practically impossible to eliminate every single risk, according to the guide?
options: It is practically and financially impossible; an acceptable risk level must be defined instead
Because all risks are always equally severe
Because risks are randomly generated and unpredictable
questions.explanation: Har risk ko eliminate karna practically/financially impossible hai — business decision hai, acceptable risk level define karna zaroori hai.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the risk management framework cycle, according to the guide?
questions.explanation: Risk Assessment → Treatment → Monitoring → Repeat — yeh cyclical framework guide mein specifically diya gaya hai.

questions.question: A company decides to purchase cyber insurance instead of spending heavily to fully prevent a low-probability, high-cost risk. Which risk treatment strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Transfer karo (insurance) — yeh risk ko kisi third party ko transfer karna hai, exactly jaise cyber insurance karti hai.

questions.question: What does compliance mean in cybersecurity?
options: Personally choosing your own preferred security tools
Following laws and standards as a legal obligation
Only applies to government agencies, never businesses
questions.explanation: Laws aur standards follow karna — legal obligation, jaise GDPR, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2.

questions.question: Which compliance standard specifically protects credit card data?
questions.explanation: PCI-DSS: Credit card data. GDPR: EU data privacy. HIPAA: US healthcare data — sab alag domains cover karte hain.

questions.question: What critical distinction does the guide make between compliance and real security?
options: Compliance is always identical to real security, with no difference at all
Compliance means a company can never be breached
Compliance is more important than actual security in every scenario
Compliance is only a minimum bar; a compliant system can still be insecure
questions.explanation: Critical distinction! Compliant system can still be insecure. Compliance is minimum bar. Many breached companies were 'compliant.'

questions.question: How severe can GDPR fines be, according to the guide?
options: A flat $100 fee regardless of company size
There are no financial penalties under GDPR
Fines apply only to companies based in the EU, never elsewhere
questions.explanation: GDPR: EU data privacy (fines up to 4% revenue) — yeh ek significant financial risk hai non-compliant companies ke liye.

questions.question: A company passes all its official PCI-DSS compliance audits, yet still suffers a major data breach shortly afterward due to a security gap the audit didn't cover. What does this illustrate?
options: Compliance and security are always exactly the same thing
Compliance is a minimum bar, not a guarantee of actual security
The breach must have been the auditor's direct fault legally
PCI-DSS audits are always 100% accurate and thorough
questions.explanation: Guide explicitly warns — many breached companies were 'compliant.' Compliance ≠ Security, yeh critical distinction hai.

questions.question: What does cyber insurance typically cover?
options: Free antivirus software for all employees
Ransomware payments, breach notification costs, legal fees, and business interruption
questions.explanation: Ransomware payment, data breach notification costs, legal fees, business interruption, regulatory fines, PR/crisis management.

questions.question: What do insurers increasingly require before issuing a cyber insurance policy, according to the guide?
options: A public disclosure of the company's source code
MFA, EDR, and backups being mandatory in place
A guarantee of zero prior security incidents ever
questions.explanation: Insurers ab MFA, EDR, backups mandatory require karte hain policy ke liye — poor security = no insurance ya very high premium.

questions.question: Why has cyber insurance premium been increasing significantly, according to the guide?
options: Due to the surge in ransomware attacks
Because compliance requirements have been removed
Due to fewer companies buying policies
questions.explanation: Premium increasingly expensive — ransomware surge se, insurers ko zyada claims handle karne padte hain.

questions.question: A company applies for cyber insurance but is denied coverage because it doesn't use MFA or maintain regular backups. What does this reflect about the insurance industry today?
options: Insurers no longer offer any cyber insurance products at all
MFA and backups have no relevance to insurance decisions
Insurers now require baseline security practices before offering coverage
This company will automatically be exempt from all cyberattacks
questions.explanation: Poor security = no insurance ya very high premium — insurers ne apni requirements tighten kar di hain ransomware surge ki wajah se.

questions.question: Besides ransomware payments, what other cost category does cyber insurance help cover, according to the guide?
questions.explanation: Ransomware payment, data breach notification costs, legal fees, business interruption, regulatory fines, PR/crisis management — sab cover hota hai.

questions.question: How does the guide define a 'Vulnerability' in cybersecurity terminology?
options: An actual code or method used to exploit a weakness
A weakness, such as unpatched software or a misconfiguration
A public database listing known attackers
The potential for harm from an attacker wanting to cause damage
questions.explanation: Vulnerability: weakness (unpatched software, misconfiguration). Threat: potential for harm. Exploit: actual code/method to use the vulnerability.

questions.question: What does CVE stand for?
questions.explanation: CVE: Common Vulnerabilities & Exposures — public database jahan known vulnerabilities track ki jaati hain.

questions.question: What was the CVSS score of CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell), the vulnerability described as literally maximum severity?
questions.explanation: CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) = 10/10 — literally maximum severity, yeh guide mein specifically iska example diya gaya hai.

questions.question: What CVSS score range does the guide say counts as 'Critical'?
questions.explanation: 0-10 severity rating. 9.0+ = Critical — patching priority = CVSS score, higher score means more urgent.

questions.question: A security researcher discovers a weakness in a company's software but has no code yet to actually take advantage of it. In the guide's terminology, what has been found so far?
options: A vulnerability, but not yet an exploit
An exploit, but not yet a vulnerability
A CVE score of exactly zero
questions.explanation: Vulnerability = weakness itself. Exploit = actual code/method to use the vulnerability — dono alag concepts hain.

questions.question: What is Penetration Testing?
options: Company-authorized security professionals attacking systems to find weaknesses before real attackers do
A method for training employees on phishing awareness only
A tool for encrypting sensitive files
An unauthorized attack carried out by criminals
questions.explanation: Company authorize karta hai security professionals ko attack karne ke liye — vulnerabilities find karo before real attackers do.

questions.question: Which analogy does the guide use for penetration testing?
options: A bank legally telling a security expert to 'try to rob us' and fixing the gaps found
A postman opening and reading letters
A movie ticket used once for entry
A smoke detector alerting to danger
questions.explanation: Bank apne security expert ko bolti hai 'try to rob us' — legally. Expert koshish karta hai, gaps dhundhta hai, fix hote hain before real robber try kare.

questions.question: Which penetration testing type gives the tester no prior information about the target, making it more realistic?
questions.explanation: Black Box: No prior info (realistic). White Box: full access/info given. Grey Box: partial info.

questions.question: What term describes penetration testers who are authorized to legally test a system's security?
questions.explanation: Ethical hackers = white hat hackers — legally authorized to find vulnerabilities before criminals do.

questions.question: A company hires a firm and gives them full internal documentation, source code, and architecture diagrams to test the system as thoroughly as possible. Which type of penetration test is this?
questions.explanation: White Box: Full access/info given — jitna zyada info tester ke paas hai, utna thorough test possible hai.

questions.question: What is Cyber Resilience, as distinct from prevention?
options: The ability to survive an attack and recover quickly, assuming a breach will happen
A tool for encrypting network traffic
Only about preventing every attack from ever happening
questions.explanation: Prevention = attack hone mat do. Resilience = attack hone ke baad bhi business continue karo, jaldi recover karo — 'assume breach' philosophy.

questions.question: Which of these is listed as a component of cyber resilience, according to the guide?
questions.explanation: Components: Incident Response plan, backups, disaster recovery, business continuity plan, crisis communication, lessons learned.

questions.question: What does RTO (Recovery Time Objective) define?
options: The length of a penetration test
The number of employees affected by an attack
The target time within which systems should be restored after an incident
The total cost of a data breach
questions.explanation: RTO (Recovery Time Objective) aur RPO define karo — RTO specifically restore hone ke liye target time define karta hai.

questions.question: What modern philosophy does the guide say drives cyber resilience thinking?
options: 'Assume breach' — it WILL happen, so be ready
'Never trust anyone, including your own IT team'
'Only focus on prevention, never on recovery'
questions.explanation: Modern philosophy: 'assume breach' — it WILL happen, be ready, isliye resilience prevention jitna hi important hai.

questions.question: After a ransomware attack, a company restores full operations within hours because it had a tested incident response plan, offline backups, and a clear business continuity strategy. What does this demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Attack hone ke baad bhi business jaldi continue karna — exactly cyber resilience ka goal hai, prevention se alag.

questions.question: What does CTI (Cyber Threat Intelligence) provide?
options: Actionable, collected information about threat actors and their tactics, for proactive defense
A backup solution for critical files
A tool for encrypting company emails
questions.explanation: Threat actors, their tactics, techniques, procedures (TTPs), indicators of compromise (IoCs) ke baare mein collected aur analyzed information.

questions.question: Which type of CTI is aimed at board-level, strategic risk decisions?
questions.explanation: Strategic (board level — risk decisions), Operational (active campaigns), Tactical (specific TTPs), Technical (IPs, hashes, domains).

questions.question: Which type of CTI deals with specific technical indicators like IPs, hashes, and domains?
questions.explanation: Technical (SOC — IPs, hashes, domains) — yeh sabse granular level hai, SOC analysts ke liye directly usable.

questions.question: What does TTP stand for in the context of Cyber Threat Intelligence?
questions.explanation: TTPs (tactics, techniques, procedures) — threat actors ke behavior patterns document karne ka standard tareeka.

questions.question: A security team receives a report listing specific malicious IP addresses and file hashes seen in a recent campaign, which they immediately load into their SIEM to block. What level of CTI did they use?
options: None of these, this is just antivirus data
questions.explanation: IPs, hashes, domains — yeh Technical CTI ka scope hai, directly SOC tools mein usable hota hai.

questions.question: What is Cyber Crime?
options: Only refers to physical theft of computer hardware
Illegal activities carried out through computers or the internet
questions.explanation: Computer ya internet ke through illegal activities — financial fraud, identity theft, ransomware, hacking, dark web markets, cyber stalking.

questions.question: What is the estimated global annual cost of cybercrime in 2023, according to the guide?
questions.explanation: $8 trillion+ global annual cost (2023) — yeh cybercrime ki scale ko dikhata hai global economy pe.

questions.question: Which Indian law covers cyber crimes, according to the guide?
options: The Indian Penal Code alone, without any IT-specific law
questions.explanation: IT Act 2000 (amended 2008) covers cyber crimes in India — cyber cells in major cities handle enforcement.

questions.question: Where does the guide say cyber crime incidents can be reported in India?
options: A local police station only, no online option exists
questions.explanation: Incidents report karo: cybercrime.gov.in — India mein official reporting portal jo guide mein mention kiya gaya hai.

questions.question: According to the guide, which IT Act section deals with unauthorized access?
questions.explanation: Section 66 = unauthorized access, Section 67 = obscene content — yeh specific sections guide mein cite kiye gaye hain.

questions.question: What is Cyber Bullying?
options: Online harassment, threatening, or humiliation carried out via digital platforms
A defensive tool that blocks unwanted network traffic
A type of encryption used in social media apps
A type of penetration test done for training purposes
questions.explanation: Digital platforms pe harassment, threatening, humiliation — social media, gaming, messaging apps ke through hoti hai.

questions.question: What is 'doxxing', as mentioned in the guide's discussion of cyber bullying?
options: Sending an encrypted message to a friend
A method for securely backing up data
Publishing someone's private information publicly without consent
A type of penetration testing technique
questions.explanation: Doxxing (private info public karna), revenge porn, trolling, fake profiles — sab cyber bullying ke forms hain.

questions.question: What does the guide recommend as a first step if you experience cyber bullying?
options: Ignore it completely and never report it
Immediately delete all your social media accounts permanently
Confront the bully in person alone
questions.explanation: Screenshots rakho evidence ke liye, platform report karo, cyber cell complaint karo — yeh recommended steps hain.

questions.question: What kind of consequences does the guide highlight as resulting from cyber bullying?
options: Only minor inconvenience with no lasting impact
Only affects the bully, not the victim
questions.explanation: Serious mental health consequences — guide is impact ko explicitly highlight karti hai, halka mudda nahi hai.

questions.question: Someone's private address and phone number are posted publicly online without their consent, as part of an ongoing harassment campaign. What specific tactic does this represent?
questions.explanation: Private info public karna bina consent ke — exactly doxxing ki definition hai, cyber bullying ka ek severe form.

questions.question: What is Digital Forensics?
options: A method for training employees on phishing awareness
Collecting, preserving, and analyzing digital evidence after an incident, for possible use in court
A tool for automatically blocking malware in real time
questions.explanation: Incident ke baad digital evidence collect, preserve, analyze, aur present karna — court mein use hone ke liye — disk images, memory dumps, network logs sab include.

questions.question: What is a 'write blocker' used for in digital forensics?
options: Preventing any accidental modification to the original evidence during analysis
Blocking all outgoing network traffic permanently
questions.explanation: Write blockers use karo, hashes verify karo, chain of custody maintain karo — evidence ka original tamper nahi hona chahiye.

questions.question: What happens to tampered digital evidence in a court proceeding, according to the guide?
options: It is automatically considered stronger proof
It is used exactly the same as untampered evidence
It is destroyed by the court immediately
questions.explanation: Tampered evidence court mein inadmissible hai — isliye evidence integrity maintain karna critical hai.

questions.question: Besides disk images, what other type of digital evidence does the guide mention forensic investigators collect?
options: Only social media likes and shares
Only physical photographs of the server room
questions.explanation: Disk images, memory dumps, network logs, deleted file recovery — sab forensic evidence collection ke part hain.

questions.question: An investigator makes a forensic copy of a compromised server's hard drive and works only on that copy, never touching the original, while documenting every handling step. What core principle is being followed?
options: Maintaining evidence integrity through chain of custody
questions.explanation: Original kabhi touch nahi — sirf forensic copy pe kaam karo, evidence integrity aur chain of custody maintain karna key principle hai.
